answer: Divergent-Sequence Identity Anchor. Each identity must produce a unique, history-dependent sequence of signed responses; new identities inherit a random starting seed. Enforcement: two clones sharing a seed can only emit identical sequences, so any attempt to diverge reveals the fork. A global violet marker flags a cloned seed on first divergence. The attacker’s cost is losing every clone at once the moment one whispers a differing response—collapsing the whole sybil set, not just one node.
